title: Catalog API pagination contract decision
purpose: Document the two competing Catalog API pagination drafts and record that the authoritative contract remains unselected pending a human choice.

scope.text: Draft A and draft B propose competing pagination contracts for GET /v1/items.
Draft A combines a JSON object response containing items and next_cursor with UI support for moving to the next page.
Draft B uses a top-level JSON array and page and page_size query parameters.

requirements.text: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

stories.text: If a human selects draft A, GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string, and the UI supports moving to the next page.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft A, when GET /v1/items succeeds, then the response is a JSON object with an items array and a next_cursor string.
Given a human has selected draft A, when the UI displays items, then a user can move to the next page.

stories.text: If a human selects draft B, GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft B, when GET /v1/items is requested, then the response body is a top-level JSON array.
Given a human has selected draft B, when GET /v1/items is requested with page and page_size, then the request URL contains page and page_size as query parameters.

edge_cases.text: Draft A does not specify the terminal value of next_cursor or how the UI determines that there is no next page.
Draft B does not specify default values, upper bounds, or validation behavior for page and page_size.
Neither draft specifies error behavior for invalid pagination parameters or cursors.

dependencies.text: Neither draft is approved; the authoritative contract has not been selected.
A human must select draft A or draft B before the corresponding alternative story is treated as an agreed deliverable.

risks.text: Draft A and draft B define incompatible GET /v1/items response shapes and pagination inputs.

Selecting draft A would not satisfy draft B's top-level-array response and page/page_size query-parameter behavior; selecting draft B would not satisfy draft A's object response, next_cursor field, and UI next-page support.
Implementing either draft before a human selection may require rework because neither draft is approved.

success_metrics.text: A recorded human selection identifies either draft A or draft B as the authoritative contract.
The selected draft's response shape and pagination behavior are checked against that draft's conditional acceptance criteria.

open_questions: Which draft, draft A or draft B, should be selected as the authoritative contract for GET /v1/items?
Who has authority to select the authoritative Catalog API contract?
If draft A is selected, what terminal next_cursor value or end-of-pagination behavior should apply?
If draft B is selected, what defaults, maximums, and validation rules apply to page and page_size?
If draft B is selected, should the UI still support moving to the next page, which is requested in draft A?
